summary: Demo of the Redwood Console FinOps panel focusing on per-route dashboards, cost breakdowns, and Optimize recommendations. Customer interested in pilot on dedicated capacity with VPC and audit/KMS requirements.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-07
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Tran (Redwood AE), Marco Reyes (Redwood SE), Janelle Park (CTO - Harbor), Ravi Kumar (Platform), Olivia Chen (SRE), Ben Carter (Product)

[00:00] Alicia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Alicia, AE on the Redwood team, and Marco our solutions engineer will walk through the console. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Janelle: Good, thanks. We've been wanting a clearer way to see per-route spend. Our finance team keeps asking how embedding calls are ballooning costs.
[00:18] Alicia: Totally — that's exactly what we'll demo today, per-route telemetry, cost breakouts, and some Optimize suggestions that can reduce unit economics.
[00:26] Marco: Hi all. I'll share my screen in a sec. For context, can you confirm your current setup? Are you running in cloud hosted endpoints or self-hosted?
[00:36] Ravi: We're mostly on GCP, using a mix of managed endpoints and some self-managed GPU infra. We do not have a private VPC for inference yet; that's a likely requirement for a pilot.
[00:45] Olivia: Also SOC2 is a must and we use GCP KMS. Audit logs, SSO/SAML, RBAC — those are checklist items.
[00:54] Marco: Great, all standard. Redwood supports VPC private control plane and KMS integrations; we have SOC2 compliance artifacts we'll share.
[01:02] Ben: Our main questions: how do you calculate per-route cost? Can we attribute cost to product teams? And how do you handle fallback models when capacity spikes?
[01:12] Marco: Short answer: per-route attribution is via route tags and model choice, with token-level cost and latency broken down across model, batch, and cache hit rates. Fallbacks use routing policies — can route to lower-cost variants or different regions. I'll show a demo.
[01:25] [Screen share starts — Marco walks through Console]
[01:33] Marco: Here's the FinOps panel. Up top is overall spend trend. Down here we have a per-route table — each route shows requests, median latency, p50/p95, token count, and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:45] Marco: Notice this route 'chat-support' — high token variance. You'll see we break cost into compute, model licensing (if any), and network. There is also an Optimize recommendation — it suggests prefix caching for this route, which would cut tokenized volume by ~30% in similar workloads.
[02:02] Ravi: How accurate are those savings estimates? They look optimistic.
[02:06] Marco: They're modelled from workload profile — sequence length distribution, cacheable prefix ratio, and our in-prod benchmarks. They're estimates, not guarantees; we run a pilot to validate.
[02:18] Olivia: What about batching? Our latency SLO is 150ms p95. Batching could hurt that.
[02:24] Marco: Right — Optimize balances batching and SLOs. We recommend tiny continuous batches for hot routes and larger batches for background jobs. The console sim shows predicted latency impact if you enable each suggestion.
[02:36] [03:00] Speaker 1: There's also a per-route heatmap — you can filter by team tag or label.
[03:06] Alicia: To add, you can export route-level cost to your billing system or map it to team codes for chargeback.
[03:12] Ben: Can we tag routes by product area automatically from our gateway?
[03:16] Marco: Yes, tags can be passed via headers or pulled from service registry. We have examples in the onboarding guide.
[03:25] Janelle: What about dedicated capacity costs? I want predictable throughput for peak trading hours.
[03:31] Marco: Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools. In the console you can compare hosted per-token spend vs estimated committed cost. There's a breakeven calculator — put in your RPS and token lengths and it estimates months to recoup reservation.
[03:46] Ravi: Any support for mixed routing? e.g., critical routes on dedicated and others on hosted?
[03:51] Marco: Absolutely. Smart routing policies let you pin a route to dedicated, with automatic fallback to hosted when dedicated is full or for overflow. You can set priority tiers.
[04:00] Olivia: On security — audit logs, retention, and who has console access?
[04:05] Alicia: RBAC supports granular roles and SSO via SAML. Audit logs stream to your SIEM, and we keep immutable request logs you can route to your storage. We'll share the SOC2 and logs spec in the follow-up.
[04:18] [04:45] Marco: Now I'll open a per-route detail for 'translate-batch' — here you see token distribution, cache hit rate, and a chart of cost by model variant. Notice a spike where the route used a larger model variant; we recommend a smaller quantized variant for that route with similar quality.
[05:00] Ravi: How does quantized model performance compare for us? We're sensitive to hallucinations on certain prompts.
[05:06] Marco: We run evals against your prompt set during onboarding. Optimize will suggest quantization profiles and runs regression tests on a prompt suite — if quality drops beyond your threshold we won't suggest it.
[05:18] Ben: Is there an automated rollback?
[05:20] Marco: Yes — rollouts support canary, A/B, and auto-fallback policies based on error or quality regressions.
[05:29] Janelle: For the pilot, we want to see end-to-end: token costs, latency, and reliability during a week of traffic.
[05:35] Alicia: Good — typical pilot steps are: we onboard two routes, baseline metrics, run Optimize recommendations, then measure delta. Estimated 2–4 week pilot.
[05:44] Olivia: Any limit on KV cache size or eviction policies? That matters for prefix caching.
[05:50] Marco: You can configure cache size and TTL per route. We expose hit rates in the UI and show estimated cost savings from caching heatmaps.
[06:01] [06:30] Speaker 2: There's also a cost-export API; many customers pipe per-route tags to their FinOps tools.
[06:36] Alicia: Let's pause for any specific questions from infra or security teams.
[06:40] Ravi: On VPC: we need private control plane and no egress of payloads outside our network except to the compute nodes in our VPC. How strict can that be?
[06:49] Marco: The Private deployment supports a customer-managed control plane in your VPC or an on-prem bundle. You can restrict egress and we integrate with customer KMS for keying; payloads remain in your environment for on-prem. For hosted, we offer enterprise contracts with dedicated tenancy and data separation.
[07:05] Janelle: Is there a cost difference for logging retention? If we keep request logs for a year that's extra.
[07:10] Alicia: Logging retention is an add-on; you can choose retention levels in the console. We'll include options in the pricing worksheet.
[07:18] Ben: How are tokens measured for multi-turn chat?
[07:22] Marco: We report both input and output tokens and maintain KV cache reuse stats. The console shows effective tokens per response after cache hits.
[07:32] [08:00] Marco: Now demoing the Optimize recommendations page — it aggregates suggestions across routes: caching, model downgrades, batch profiles, and quantization. Each suggestion shows estimated monthly $$ savings and expected latency delta.
[08:14] Ravi: Are these savings net of added engineering effort?
[08:17] Marco: The UI shows estimated engineering time as a field (low/med/high) — it's heuristic but helps prioritization.
[08:25] Janelle: Can we run a fully managed change where Redwood applies config changes?
[08:29] Marco: Yes, for enterprise plans we offer change management: Redwood operations can apply and monitor changes under an agreed runbook.
[08:36] Olivia: Do you support model-specific latency SLOs? For ex. p95 < 250ms for gpt-style models?
[08:41] Marco: You set SLOs per route and per model family. The runtime enforces them with priority scheduling and preemptive routing.
[08:48] Ben: Any details on how fallbacks affect user experience? If fallback model is lower-quality, can we do partial degrade — e.g., shorten responses rather than switch model?
[08:57] Marco: Good question — we support graceful degradation strategies: reduce max tokens, shorten summaries, or switch to a cheaper model variant with a template that reduces hallucination risk.
[09:09] [09:30] Speaker 1: There's a demo of a canary deploy with automatic rollback after a regression was detected on the eval set.
[09:37] Alicia: Back to next steps — we'll need your two routes and sample payloads to create the pilot baseline. Marco will run the perf test with a 512-token representative sample.
[09:47] Ravi: We can provide those. Also expect firewall/IP allowlist requirements.
[09:51] Marco: We'll send the allowlist and onboarding checklist.
[10:00] [10:45] Ben: On pricing — can you outline the structure? Per-token for hosted, plus reserved capacity for Dedicated?
[10:52] Alicia: Exactly. Hosted is per-token + model delta. Dedicated is a monthly committed capacity fee with effective lower per-token costs for heavy usage. We also have add-ons for logs retention, premium SLAs, and private deployments. I'll send a tailored worksheet for your traffic profile.
[11:10] Janelle: Any references of similar customers who've run FinOps across routes?
[11:14] Alicia: Yes, we'll share two case studies where customers reduced spend by 25–40% by applying caching and quantized variants on background routes.
[11:23] Olivia: Would it be possible to get a sandbox account to poke around the console ourselves?
[11:27] Alicia: Yes, we'll provision a sandbox with read-only access to the console and a test model. We'll also share the sample dashboard we've been showing.
[11:36] [12:00] Marco: Quick note on telemetry: we ingest route tags, model name, tokens, latency, status codes — and we correlate anomalies with infra events. The UI surfaces anomaly detection for sudden token spikes.
[12:14] Ravi: Good — that's been a pain point for us.
[12:18] Ben: Do you capture per-token costs when using third-party model licensing?
[12:22] Marco: Yes, the console allows you to define model economics — if a model has a licensing fee we amortize that into per-token cost displayed.
[12:30] [13:00] Janelle: Any caveats on regional routing? We have EU data residency needs.
[13:06] Alicia: You can pin routes to region-specific capacity. For strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with region-specific pools.
[13:16] Olivia: For the pilot, we'd prefer dedicated capacity in us-west1 but with log export to our GCS.
[13:21] Marco: That works — we'll include that pattern in the onboarding doc.
[13:30] [14:00] Speaker 2: There's a spreadsheet with projected savings per suggestion — we'll attach it.
[14:06] Alicia: Okay, wrapping — to confirm action items: Alicia sends pricing and security docs, Marco runs the baseline, Harbor provides two routes and payloads and network allowlist. Pilot kickoff week of 12/20. Anything else?
[14:24] Janelle: Please include sample SLO configs and an example rollback policy.
[14:29] Marco: Will do.
[14:33] Ben: And the sandbox read-only link.
[14:35] Alicia: Yep, sandbox and dashboard link.
[14:38] [15:00] End notes: meeting ends with quick thanks.

Recap (verbatim):
- Objective: Validate per-route cost control and run pilot on dedicated capacity with VPC/KMS and SOC2 artifacts.
- Next: Pricing + security docs, baseline perf, sample payloads, pilot scheduling.

References shared during call:
- Console FinOps panel (live demo)
- Benchmark spreadsheet (link will be provided)
- SOC2 + KMS integration guide (to be shared)

Transcript ends.
